title: Assemble the reference list into the manuscript and reconcile citations both ways
description:
Live issue L2. BLOCKS SUBMISSION. REFERENCES.md and REFERENCES-verified.md exist at the manuscript root but no '# References' heading appears anywhere in output/manuscript-assembled.md. Every in-text author-date citation is therefore unresolvable by a referee.

Done when: REFERENCES.md is assembled into the manuscript, every in-text author-date resolves to an entry, and every entry is cited at least once.

Also resolve the [secondary] entries: REFERENCES.md marks several works as known only as MMAF (2022) prints them, with bibliographic details reproduced rather than verified. Marine Policy will want those either obtained at source or explicitly flagged. And apply the four wrong filename years recorded in REFERENCES-verified.md - do not cite any of them from the filename.

Do after the literature task, which will add entries. See 04-manuscript/output/CONSOLIDATED-REVIEW.md

title: Rebuild the word-count cut plan against the drafted text and execute it
description:
Live issue L1. BLOCKS SUBMISSION. Main text is 17,169 words against the Marine Policy target of 9,000-10,000 (PRD lines 220-221). Required cut is roughly 7,000 words.

The archived 04-manuscript/archive/CUT-LIST.md finds only ~1,770 words - four times too small - and was written against SOT revision 1, before sections 5 (15.4 KB), 7 (20.1 KB) and 9 (10.7 KB) reached their present size. Section 7 is now the largest in the paper.

Carry forward the archived plan's protected list, which still holds: the section 4 maturity qualifications, the 34/1 pairing, the loadings-versus-contributions caveat, every flagged concession, and section 8.5's limitations must not be cut. Also preserve the renormalisation test that bounds the weight ambiguity at under 0.1 percentage points - it closes referee M3 and is the manuscript's strongest verification asset.

Done when: a fresh cut plan exists against the drafted text and main text is within 9,000-10,000 words. See 04-manuscript/output/CONSOLIDATED-REVIEW.md

title: Decide the figures - five are built and none is cited
description:
Live issue L3. figures/ holds fig1-compilation-chain, fig2-leverage-inversion, fig3-weight-cascade, fig5-indicator-mapping-matrix and fig6-reporting-calendar as HTML. Referee C1 (four cited figures did not exist) was closed by STRIKING all four citations, leaving the paper with zero display figures and five orphaned assets. Marine Policy imposes no Nature-style 4-6 display-item cap, so the striking conceded more than the venue required.

Decide explicitly, either: (a) reinstate a subset with legends stating that shares are this study's products of published percentages and are indicative - fig5-indicator-mapping-matrix is the strongest candidate since the mapping IS the contribution; or (b) retire all five to figures/archive/ with a note so the absence is a decision rather than an oversight.

Do after the cut plan, since a cut section may remove a figure's referent. Note the gap numbering (no fig4) suggests the set was already being pruned. See 04-manuscript/output/CONSOLIDATED-REVIEW.md

title: Source composite-indicator methodology literature and engage contradicting work in section 9
description:
Live issue L4 (referee M9, unfixed). Sections 8-9 cite only three external works, all supportive: United Nations et al. 2024, Rahayu et al. 2024, Gacutan et al. 2022. REFERENCES-verified.md independently records the cause as 'the remaining hole': no composite-indicator methodology literature exists in the project document set - no OECD/JRC Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators, no Ocean Health Index or comparable, nothing on weighting-scheme sensitivity, PCA-derived weights, or imputation inside composite indices.

Why it matters: without it the Introduction cannot establish that the IBEI's construction is a recognised class of problem rather than an idiosyncratic Indonesian one, which is the move that licenses the novelty claim. Section 8.3's variance-weighting argument has the same exposure.

Do this FIRST: it is the only live item needing new reading, it may ADD words, and the word-count cut plan must be built knowing its cost. Not blocked by the no-agency-engagement constraint.

Done when: composite-indicator methodology literature sourced from outside the project folder, and at least two works brought into section 9 that can be read AGAINST the conclusion. See 04-manuscript/output/CONSOLIDATED-REVIEW.md

title: Re-run the pre-submission compliance pass against Marine Policy rather than Nature
description:
The archived referee report assessed the manuscript against Nature (~2,500-4,300 words, 4-6 display items, <=50 references, summary-paragraph template) and returned 'fail (3-5x over)'. The PRD names Marine Policy at 9,000-10,000 words, Harvard author-date (PRD lines 220-221, 566, 571). Against the real target the manuscript is ~1.8x over, not 5x, and several Nature-only failures do not bind at all.

Done when: a compliance table exists against Marine Policy's actual author guidelines - word limit, reference style and cap, display-item rules, abstract length and format, declarations, highlights and keywords if required. Confirm the venue decision between Marine Policy and Ocean & Coastal Management first (PRD line 684 leaves it open).

Do last, after the cut and the reference list. See 04-manuscript/output/CONSOLIDATED-REVIEW.md

title: Convert the 52 house-style tags in running prose to prose qualifiers
description:
Live issue L5. [EVIDENCE GAP] x27, [ASSUMPTION] x19, [CONTESTED DENOMINATOR] x6 remain in running prose in output/manuscript-assembled.md.

These are NOT a defect - briefs/HOUSE-STYLE-DIRECTIVE.md line 57 records [CONTESTED DENOMINATOR] as added by user ruling on 2026-08-16, and the apparatus is working as designed internally. But it cannot go to a journal.

Do this LAST, after the word-count cut. The tags mark exactly the sentences most likely to be cut, so converting first wastes the work.

Done when: every tag is converted to a prose qualifier carrying the same hedge, and no bracketed tag remains in the assembled manuscript. See 04-manuscript/output/CONSOLIDATED-REVIEW.md

title: Correct the stale Rinaldi citation year in CLAUDE.md
description:
Live issue L7. The manuscript cites 'Rinaldi et al. (2025)' three times. REFERENCES-verified.md confirms 2025 is correct - received Nov 2024, accepted Jun 2025, Malaysian Journal of Mathematical Sciences 19(4): 1471-1506, doi:10.47836/mjms.19.4.16 - and warns the filename year is wrong.

But CLAUDE.md's Evidence-precedence section refers to 'Rinaldi et al. 2024' four times.

The manuscript is right and CLAUDE.md is stale. Correct CLAUDE.md, not the manuscript. Independent of the other tasks. See 04-manuscript/output/CONSOLIDATED-REVIEW.md

title: Disambiguate Table N between this paper's display items and source-document tables
description:
Live issue L6. The manuscript uses capitalised 'Table N' for both its own display items and for tables inside cited source documents. Line 347 '(MMAF, 2022, Table 5, p. 52 [pdf 66])' and line 350 'Table 6 (p. 53 [pdf 67])' cite the pilot report's tables, whilst lines 500, 563 and 611 cite this paper's Table 3. Juknis tables are correctly disambiguated as 'Tabel'; MMAF's are not.

This initially reads as a figure-citation-order violation and is NOT one - worth recording so it is not rediscovered as a defect.

Fix: cite source tables as 'MMAF (2022) tab. 5' or similar, reserving capitalised 'Table N' for this paper's own display items. Independent of the other tasks. See 04-manuscript/output/CONSOLIDATED-REVIEW.md
